patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with a history of recurrent chlamydia and PID who develops tubal factor infertility, then endometriosis treated with suppression and laparoscopy, and later a ruptured right tubal ectopic pregnancy managed with salpingectomy. Primary care carries preventive care, the referrals and the follow-up around her outside gynecology and reproductive care.

documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30 yo woman, elementary school teacher, new to the practice. Was seeing a primary care office closer to her old apartment; she and her husband bought a house in Belchertown this spring. Wants a doctor she can actually reach. Feels well, no complaints today.

PMH: chlamydia twice in her twenties, both treated at the clinic she used then. One episode of PID around 24 or 25, treated with oral antibiotics, never admitted. Periods regular, about monthly, not painful, no bleeding between. Using condoms with husband for now; they talk about kids "in a year or so."
PSH: none.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mom had endometriosis and ended up with a hysterectomy at 42. Mom's sister never could get pregnant, no cause ever found. Dad has high blood pressure.
SH: teaches 2nd grade. Never smoked. Wine once or twice a week, a glass. She told me without being asked that she used IV drugs for a stretch in her early twenties and has not since; no treatment program, no relapses. We talked about screening for HIV and hep C and she was glad to do it.

ROS: negative except as above.
Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Well appearing, relaxed. HEENT normal, no thyroid enlargement or nodules. Heart regular rate, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected, bimanual without tenderness or masses. Skin without lesions. Mood bright.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap with HPV co-test today (age 30). Tdap today, last one she can remember was high school. CBC, CMP, lipids.
2. STI history: GC/chlamydia NAAT today; HIV and hepatitis C screening given her history.
3. Remote IV drug use: in remission for many years, nothing to do beyond screening.
4. Records release signed for prior office.
Return in a year, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Melissa, everything from Tuesday is back and normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV, hepatitis C, gonorrhea and chlamydia tests were all negative. Your Pap and HPV test were normal too, so you won't need another one for five years. Nice to have you in the practice.

documents.title: RE: Your results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you so much, that's a relief. Have a good weekend!

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 23 pages: office notes 2012 to 2019, lab results, immunization record.

Summary of relevant items:
- 2012: chlamydia NAAT positive on routine screen; azithromycin given; partner notified.
- 2014: lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, treated as PID with IM ceftriaxone and two weeks of oral doxycycline; improved at recheck. Not admitted.
- 2016: chlamydia NAAT positive; treated with azithromycin; repeat test at 3 months negative.
- 2016: Pap at age 27 negative for intraepithelial lesion.
- Allergies: NKDA. No surgeries.
Immunization record shows childhood series complete; no Tdap on file after adolescence.

Scanned to chart. Reviewed by PCP; history already reflected in the problem list.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called the on-call line early this morning. Lower belly pain since Saturday, much worse overnight, fever 102 at home, threw up twice and can't keep down water or ibuprofen. Says it feels like the PID she had years ago but worse. Discussed with PCP: needs to be seen in person today and can't take pills, so ED rather than office. Husband driving her to the regional hospital ED now. Told her to call us when she's home.

documents.title: PCP addendum
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Agree. Likely PID given history, with vomiting and fever; needs IV treatment and imaging to rule out abscess. Will follow.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Gynecology
documents.author: hospital gynecology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology
Admission 04/27/2020, discharge 04/30/2020
Allergies: NKDA

Admitting diagnosis: acute pelvic inflammatory disease.
Discharge diagnosis: pelvic inflammatory disease, chlamydial.

History: 31 yo G0 with prior chlamydia and an outpatient-treated PID episode presented with two days of lower abdominal pain, fever and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. SARS-CoV-2 screening negative on arrival.

Course: T 38.6 C, HR 108 on arrival. Bilateral lower abdominal tenderness without peritonitis; cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness on bimanual. WBC 14.2. Urine hCG negative. Pelvic ultrasound without tubo-ovarian abscess. Admitted for parenteral therapy: cefoxitin 2 g IV every 6 hours plus doxycycline 100 mg every 12 hours. Afebrile by 48 hours, tolerating diet, tenderness much improved. Cervical NAAT returned positive for Chlamydia trachomatis, negative for gonorrhea.

Discharge medications: doxycycline 100 mg PO BID and metronidazole 500 mg PO BID to complete a 14-day course.
Instructions: no intercourse until treatment complete and partner treated; partner referred for treatment. Retest for chlamydia in 3 months. Follow up with PCP within one week.

Hospitalist and gynecology teams. Copy to primary care physician.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit — Post-Hospital Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from home, school is remote so she is home anyway. Discharge summary reviewed: chlamydial PID, no abscess on ultrasound, IV cefoxitin/doxy, home on doxy + metronidazole to finish 14 days.

Today day 8 of antibiotics. No fever since the hospital. Pain down to a dull ache low on both sides, maybe 2/10, using nothing for it. Eating normally. Some nausea with the metronidazole, takes it with food and it's fine. No alcohol on it. Husband was seen and treated last week.

Appears well on video, comfortable, no distress.

A/P: chlamydial PID, improving on oral therapy. Finish the course. Abstain until both done. Recheck chlamydia/gonorrhea at her physical in August (3 months). Call if fever, worsening pain or vomiting.

Discussed that repeated pelvic infections can affect the tubes and later fertility; she asked, and we left it that if pregnancy is slow to happen we evaluate early.

medications.drug_text: prenatal multivitamin with folic acid Oral Tablet

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Masks on, she's nervous about going back into a classroom in a few weeks but the district has a hybrid plan.

Interval: admitted in April with chlamydial PID, finished the 14 days of doxy/metronidazole, no pain since mid-May. Periods regular every 28-30 days, no cramping to speak of.

She and her husband have decided to stop using condoms and start trying to get pregnant this month. Asked what she should be doing. Already bought a prenatal vitamin with folic acid last week and is taking it daily.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily. NKDA.
SH: unchanged, wine maybe once a week now.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no adnexal tenderness on bimanual, no CMT.

A/P
1. PID, resolved. Repeat GC/chlamydia NAAT today (3 months post-treatment).
2. Preconception: continue prenatal vitamin with folic acid. Limit alcohol once trying. If no pregnancy after 12 months, or sooner if cycles change, we'll start an evaluation, earlier than usual given the PID history.
3. Health maintenance: Pap up to date (2019). BMP today. Flu shot in October.
Return 1 year.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your chlamydia and gonorrhea tests are negative, so the infection is cleared, and your chemistry panel is normal. Good luck to you both.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Screened at door, no COVID symptoms. Possibly pregnant? Pt says no, period started last week. Flu vaccine quadrivalent R deltoid. VIS given. No issues.

documents.title: Vaccine card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I finally got both Pfizer shots through the teacher clinic at the pharmacy, 3/11 and 4/1. Photo of my card attached so you have it. Second one knocked me out for a day, that's it.

documents.title: RE: Vaccine card
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Melissa, both doses are entered in your chart now.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for her yearly. They've been trying for a year now, since last August, timed with an ovulation app the last few months. No pregnancy, no late periods. Cycles every 28 days like clockwork, 4-5 days of bleeding, light cramps on day one only. No pelvic pain, no pain with sex. Taking the prenatal daily. Husband healthy, has never been checked. Frustrated but not down. Has had both COVID shots.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily. Allergies: NKDA.
SH: wine is down to almost none. Never smoker.

O: vitals as charted. Well. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Deferred pelvic today, normal last year.

A/P
1. Infertility, 12 months trying, age 32, regular ovulatory cycles. Given two prior chlamydia infections and PID with admission last year, tubal disease is the main concern. Referral to gynecology for infertility workup (expect HSG and semen analysis for husband). TSH and CBC today.
2. Preventive: flu shot this fall. Pap current.
PHQ-2 1. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Referral to Obstetrics & Gynecology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reason for referral: infertility, 12 months of unprotected intercourse without conception.

32 yo G0, regular 28-day cycles, no dysmenorrhea or pelvic pain. History of chlamydia x2 in her twenties, outpatient PID ~2014, and admission April 2020 for chlamydial PID (no TOA). On prenatal vitamin only. NKDA. Mother had endometriosis with hysterectomy at 42; maternal aunt with unexplained infertility.
TSH and CBC pending, will forward.

Thank you for seeing her.

documents.title: Labs and gyn referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your thyroid test and blood count are normal. The gynecology referral went out Tuesday; their office should call you to schedule. If you haven't heard in two weeks let us know.

documents.title: RE: Labs and gyn referral
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called, first appointment is October 21. Long wait but okay.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation — Infertility
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 10/21/2021
Referring: primary care physician

Reason: primary infertility.

Ms. Pereira is a 32 year old G0 who has had regular unprotected intercourse with her husband for about 14 months without a pregnancy. Menses every 28 days, normal flow. She denies intermenstrual bleeding, painful periods or pelvic pain. Prior sexually transmitted infections: chlamydia twice and an episode of PID requiring admission in 2020.

Surgical history: none.
Medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother with endometriosis, hysterectomy at 42; maternal aunt with infertility of unknown cause; father hypertensive.
Social: second-grade teacher. Never smoker. Occasional wine.

Exam: well woman, normal vitals. Abdomen benign. Normal external genitalia and vagina, cervix without lesions, uterus normal size and mobile, no adnexal masses or tenderness.

Hysterosalpingogram performed in our office today (cycle day 8): normal uterine cavity. Neither tube fills beyond the proximal segment; no intraperitoneal spill on either side.

Impression: infertility, tubal factor, with bilateral tubal occlusion on HSG, consistent with her history of pelvic infection.

Plan: referral to reproductive endocrinology to discuss options, which with both tubes blocked will center on IVF. Semen analysis for her husband will be ordered by REI. Continue prenatal vitamin.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given L deltoid. Pt asked whether flu shot is OK if she gets pregnant; told yes, recommended in pregnancy. VIS given.

documents.title: Pharmacy Immunization Notice
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Community pharmacy immunization notification. Patient: Pereira, Melissa, DOB 04/04/1989. Vaccine: COVID-19 mRNA (Pfizer-BioNTech) booster dose, 0.3 mL IM, left deltoid, administered 11/13/2021. Lot on file. No adverse event reported at 15 minutes.

documents.title: Fertility clinic
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The fertility clinic can't see me until April 20. Is there anything we should be doing in the meantime or anywhere faster? Kind of discouraged.

documents.title: RE: Fertility clinic
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry, the waits for reproductive endocrinology are long everywhere right now. Nothing medical needs to happen before then; keep taking the prenatal vitamin. Ask them to put you on the cancellation list. If you want to talk any of it through before April, book a visit or call.

documents.title: Reproductive Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: reproductive endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside reproductive endocrinology and infertility practice
Date of visit: 04/20/2022

Dear colleague,

I met Melissa and her husband today for infertility. She was referred by gynecology after about 14 months of trying; they are now at roughly 20 months. Cycles are regular, every 28 days. Her husband's semen analysis this month is normal in volume, concentration, motility and morphology.

Pertinent history: severe pelvic inflammatory disease two years ago that put her in the hospital on IV antibiotics, plus earlier chlamydia. No surgeries. Medications: prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Family history of endometriosis in her mother and infertility in a maternal aunt.

Vital signs stable. Pelvic examination unremarkable.

I reviewed the hysterosalpingogram from October: both tubes are occluded proximally with no spill.

Assessment: tubal factor infertility, bilateral, after pelvic infection. Male factor absent; ovulatory.

Recommendation: with both tubes blocked, IVF is the treatment that gives them a real chance. We went over the process, timeline, success rates at her age and her coverage. They would like time to think it over and will call us.

Reproductive endocrinology

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to let you know we met with the fertility doctor. We've decided to hold off on IVF for now, it's a lot to take on with everything this year. We may come back to it. Thank you for getting us there.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. That's a reasonable choice and the door stays open. I'm here if you want to talk it through.

orders.reason: pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia; suspected endometriosis

documents.title: Annual Physical and Pelvic Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, and she wants to talk about pain.

Since about April, aching low pelvic pain most days, a 5 out of 10 today, much worse the first 2-3 days of her period when it can keep her in bed. New this year: it hurts deep with intercourse, enough that they've mostly stopped. Around her period her stools go loose, no blood, no black stool, normal between. No fever, no discharge, no urinary symptoms. Has been taking 400 mg ibuprofen OTC with partial help. LMP 7/12, normal.

After the REI visit in April they decided to hold off on IVF. She is not trying to prevent pregnancy but with blocked tubes doesn't expect one.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, OTC ibuprofen. NKDA.
FH reviewed, mother with endometriosis.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, a little tired. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic and bilateral lower quadrant tenderness, no guarding or rebound, no masses. Pelvic deferred to gyn, who she'd rather see for that.
Urine hCG negative in office.

A/P
1. Pelvic pain with dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia and cyclic loose stools, ~3 months. Pattern and family history point toward endometriosis. Not infectious by history. Start ibuprofen 600 mg q6-8h prn with food. Start a combined pill (ethinyl estradiol 20 mcg / norethindrone acetate 1 mg) taken continuously, skipping placebos, for suppression; reviewed clot warning signs, she's a nonsmoker with no migraine with aura and normal BP. Back to her gynecologist for exam and imaging.
2. Health maintenance: flu shot and updated COVID booster this fall. Pap due 2024.
PHQ-2 1.

documents.title: Pharmacy Request — Early Refill
documents.author: pharmacy
documents.body: Insurance rejecting refill of ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 as too soon (plan allows 1 pack per 28 days). Patient taking continuously, needs 1 pack per 21 days. Please submit quantity override or rewrite sig.

documents.title: Quantity Override Submitted
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called PPO pharmacy benefit line. Quantity override requested for continuous use, dx pelvic pain/suspected endometriosis. Approved for 13 packs per year through 08/2023. Pharmacy notified, filling today.

documents.title: Pain
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update: two months on the continuous pill and the 600s. Honestly maybe a little better but not much, still having bad days. Gyn appointment is Oct 24. Should I do anything different before then?

documents.title: RE: Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. Stay the course until gyn sees you; they'll examine you and likely get an ultrasound. Make sure you're taking ibuprofen with food, and not more than 4 doses a day. Fever, vomiting or pain that's suddenly much worse means call us the same day.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound. Uterus retroverted, normal in size and contour, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin and uniform. Right ovary normal in size with normal follicles. Left ovary normal in size with normal follicles. No adnexal mass or cyst. No hydrosalpinx. No free fluid.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-Up — Chronic Pelvic Pain
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 10/24/2022

Melissa returns, seen last year for infertility (tubal factor, bilateral occlusion on HSG), now with half a year of pelvic pain that peaks with her periods. She describes deep pain with intercourse and loose, non-bloody stools that come and go with her cycle. For the past three months she has been on ibuprofen and a continuous combined pill started by her PCP, with little benefit.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 continuously, ibuprofen 600 mg as needed, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Vitals normal. Abdomen soft without peritoneal signs. Speculum normal. Bimanual: retroverted uterus; tenderness in the posterior cul-de-sac; no adnexal mass.

CBC and inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) normal. Transvaginal ultrasound today normal.

Assessment: chronic pelvic pain with dysmenorrhea, deep dyspareunia and cyclic bowel symptoms, consistent with endometriosis (clinical diagnosis; strong family history). Normal imaging does not exclude it.

Plan: continue continuous combined pill and ibuprofen for now; recheck in about six months. If pain persists, diagnostic laparoscopy for diagnosis and excision.

OB/GYN

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza (L deltoid) and Pfizer bivalent booster (R deltoid). VIS and EUA fact sheet given. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Refill Request — Ibuprofen
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called on lunch break for ibuprofen 600 refill. Uses it most days of her period plus a few other days a month, always with food. No stomach pain, no black stools. Still on the continuous pill. Refill sent per protocol, #60 with 2 refills. Gyn recheck is in April.

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound. Uterus retroverted, normal in size, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin. Right ovary normal in size containing several small round cysts with homogeneous low-level internal echoes, the largest 1.8 cm, without internal vascularity. Left ovary normal in size with similar small cysts, the largest 1.4 cm, without internal vascularity. No solid component in either ovary. No hydrosalpinx. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Small bilateral ovarian cysts with the appearance of endometriomas ("chocolate cysts"), largest 1.8 cm on the right and 1.4 cm on the left.

documents.title: Gynecology Follow-Up — Endometriosis
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 04/13/2023

Follow-up of endometriosis (clinical diagnosis 10/2022) and bilateral tubal factor infertility. Seen by a different physician in the group today.

Despite six months more of the continuous pill and ibuprofen her pain has steadily worsened. Breakthrough bleeding every few weeks brings severe cramping, intercourse remains painful, and she describes missing work days and avoiding activities she used to enjoy. She and her husband still hope to have a child one day.

Meds: ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 1/20 continuously, ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: retroverted uterus; tenderness in the posterior cul-de-sac on bimanual; no palpable adnexal mass.

Labs today: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.5, ESR 20, CA-125 58 (elevated).
Transvaginal ultrasound: several small cysts in both ovaries with the typical appearance of endometriomas.

Assessment: endometriosis with progressive pelvic pain on first-line suppression, now with small bilateral endometriomas and an elevated CA-125 that fits that picture.

Plan: diagnostic and operative laparoscopy to confirm the diagnosis, excise implants and free adhesions, and assess the tubes with dye. Consent discussed; she wants to schedule it for the end of the school year. Continue current medications until surgery.

OB/GYN

documents.title: Surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My laparoscopy is booked for June 27, right after school lets out. Do I need a pre-op visit with you or bloodwork from your office?

documents.title: RE: Surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: For a healthy person having an outpatient laparoscopy the surgical center's pre-admission team handles what's needed, and you're up to date with us. If they ask for a clearance letter, send me the form. Hoping this gives you some relief.

reports.text:
Specimens: (A) peritoneum, posterior cul-de-sac, excision; (B) pelvic peritoneum, right pelvic sidewall, excision.
Gross: A, two tan-red fibrous tissue fragments, 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.3 cm in aggregate. B, one tan fibrous fragment, 1.1 x 0.5 x 0.2 cm. Entirely submitted.
Microscopic: both specimens show endometrial-type glands with surrounding endometrial stroma within fibrotic peritoneal tissue, with hemosiderin-laden macrophages. No atypia. No malignancy.
reports.conclusion: A and B: endometriosis. Negative for malignancy.

procedures.procedure: Laparoscopy with excision of endometriosis implants and lysis of pelvic adhesions

documents.title: Operative Report — Laparoscopy
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outpatient surgery center, gynecology
Date of surgery: 06/27/2023
Preoperative diagnosis: endometriosis, chronic pelvic pain, bilateral tubal factor infertility.
Postoperative diagnosis: same, confirmed; pelvic adhesions.
Procedure: diagnostic laparoscopy, excision of endometriosis implants, lysis of pelvic adhesions, chromopertubation.
Anesthesia: general. EBL minimal. Complications: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: retroverted uterus of normal size. Endometriosis implants on the peritoneum of the posterior cul-de-sac and right pelvic sidewall. Both ovaries normal in size, each with small endometriomas, left in place to preserve ovarian reserve. Filmy adhesions around both tubes and adnexa. Upper abdomen normal.

Description: umbilical entry and two lower ports. Adhesions lysed sharply, freeing both adnexa. Implants excised with margins and sent to pathology. Chromopertubation with dilute indigo carmine after adhesiolysis: the right tube filled and spilled freely; the left tube did not fill. Hemostasis assured, ports closed.

Disposition: discharged home the same day.
Pathology: endometriosis in both specimens.
Follow-up: office in 6 weeks.

medications.drug_text: ethinyl estradiol 0.02 MG / norethindrone acetate 1 MG Oral Tablet
medications.reason: Stopped by gynecology after laparoscopy to allow conception

documents.title: Gynecology Post-Operative Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 08/09/2023

Six weeks after laparoscopy with excision of endometriosis and adhesiolysis. Incisions healed. Pain much better than before surgery. Pathology confirmed endometriosis.

We reviewed that at surgery the right tube opened with dye after the adhesions were freed, while the left remained blocked. She and her husband would like to try to conceive on their own for now. We will stop the continuous pill today. Ibuprofen for period pain. If no pregnancy in 6 to 12 months, return to reproductive endocrinology.

Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
OB/GYN

orders.order: Return visit in 6 months, pelvic pain follow-up

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, few days before teachers go back.

Interval: laparoscopy 6/27, endometriosis confirmed on pathology, implants excised, adhesions freed. Gyn op note says right tube open on dye, left still blocked. Post-op visit 8/9: off the continuous pill now, they're going to try on their own for 6-12 months, then back to REI if needed.

Feels like a different person. Pain 1/10 today, "the everyday ache is gone." First period off the pill came last week, crampy for a day, ibuprofen covered it. Intercourse comfortable again.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, cheerful. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, three small healed port scars, nontender.

A/P
1. Endometriosis s/p laparoscopic excision and adhesiolysis 6/2023, pain much improved. Off hormonal suppression to try to conceive. Ibuprofen prn. Med list updated.
2. Tubal factor infertility: per gyn, right tube patent after surgery. Continue prenatal.
3. Health maintenance: CBC/CMP. Flu and COVID this fall. Pap due next year.
Check in around February, sooner if pain returns.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count, kidney and liver tests from Tuesday are all normal. Have a good first week back.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pregnancy screen: LMP 10/3, pt reports no chance she's late. Flu vaccine L arm, 2023-24 Pfizer COVID R arm. VIS sheets given. Waited 15 minutes, fine.

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, after school this year since summer got away from her.

Interval: missed the February check, messaged instead. Endometriosis pain stays controlled after last year's surgery: first day or two of each period, ibuprofen helps, no pain between, intercourse fine. Cycles regular, 28 days. Not pregnant in the 14 months since surgery; they haven't gone back to REI and aren't sure they will. No new symptoms, no discharge, no fever.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA.
SH: never smoker, a glass of wine a week or so.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, port scars healed. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected, bimanual with retroverted uterus, nontender, no masses.

A/P
1. Endometriosis, quiet on ibuprofen alone.
2. Infertility: reminded her the REI door is open; she'll think about it.
3. Preventive: Pap/HPV today (5 years). STI screening today given her history: GC/chlamydia, HIV, RPR. Lipids and CBC. Flu and 2024-25 COVID today.
PHQ-2 1. Return 1 year.

conditions.label: Chlamydial infection of lower genitourinary tract

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 7 days

orders.order: Chlamydia and gonorrhea NAAT, retest in 3 months

documents.title: Result Call — Chlamydia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt on her lunch break re: positive chlamydia NAAT from Thursday's screen. Gonorrhea, HIV and syphilis negative. She has no symptoms. Upset but took it calmly.

Plan: doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days sent. Expedited partner therapy: second doxycycline prescription for her husband under his name per state EPT guidance. No intercourse until both have finished 7 days of treatment. Retest in 3 months. Call for fever or pelvic pain; with her history I want to hear early.
Pap from 10/10 still pending.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test are normal. Next one in five years. The lab order for your recheck in January is in, just stop by any morning after the 13th.

documents.title: Other labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Did my cholesterol come back okay? And we both picked up the doxycycline Monday night.

documents.title: RE: Other labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, cholesterol and blood count are normal. Good that you both started. Take the doxycycline with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes after, and go easy on direct sun this week.

conditions.label: Chlamydial infection of lower genitourinary tract

documents.title: Specimen Collection
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt in before school for 3-month retest. Self-collected vaginal swab for GC/CT NAAT, instructions given. Sent to lab.

documents.title: Retest result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your repeat chlamydia and gonorrhea tests are negative, so the infection is cleared. Nothing else to do.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could I get a refill on the ibuprofen 600? Same as always, mostly for the first days of my period.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent to your pharmacy, 60 tablets with 2 refills. Take with food.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, back to her August slot.

Doing well. Chlamydia treated last fall, January retest negative. Endometriosis: cramps the first day or two of her period, ibuprofen takes care of it, otherwise pain free. Regular 28-day cycles. Not using any contraception; still no pregnancy, still undecided about IVF and not in a hurry to decide.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA.
SH: teaching 2nd grade again this year. Never smoker. Wine about once a week.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Neck without thyromegaly. Heart regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin normal.

A/P
1. Endometriosis, controlled with prn NSAID.
2. Tubal factor infertility, not pursuing treatment for now.
3. Preventive: Pap next due 2029. CBC/CMP today. Flu shot this fall.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1. Return 1 year.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Melissa, blood counts, kidney, liver and electrolytes are all normal.

conditions.label: Right tubal pregnancy without intrauterine pregnancy

reports.text: Transvaginal ultrasound with color Doppler. Uterus retroverted, normal in size. No intrauterine gestational sac, yolk sac or embryo; empty uterine cavity. Right adnexa: 3.0 cm complex mass separate from the right ovary, with no internal flow on color Doppler. Right ovary separately visualized with a small known endometrioma. Left ovary normal in size with small known endometrioma. Small amount of free fluid in the posterior cul-de-sac.
reports.conclusion: Positive pregnancy test with no intrauterine pregnancy and a 3 cm complex right adnexal mass with small free fluid, consistent with right ectopic pregnancy.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department
Date of service: 10/19/2025, arrived 13:20
Allergies: NKDA

CC: sudden severe right lower quadrant pain.

HPI: 36 yo G1 with endometriosis (laparoscopic excision 2023), chronic pelvic pain and tubal factor infertility, arrives with abrupt severe right lower abdominal pain starting late this morning. Two days of light intermittent vaginal spotting. LMP about 6 weeks ago; cycles regular every 28 days. Chlamydia treated a year ago. Sexually active with one partner; condoms used inconsistently.
Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin.

Exam: BP 110/70, HR 98, T 37.2 C (99.0 F). Uncomfortable, holding still. Abdomen tender in the RLQ with rebound. Pelvic: os closed, no active bleeding in the vault, cervical motion tenderness present; no adnexal mass felt.

ED course: urine hCG positive. Quantitative hCG 2,850. Hgb 11.8. Type A positive. Cervical GC/CT NAAT sent. PID entered the differential given cervical motion tenderness and her history; with a positive pregnancy test, the bedside concern shifted to ectopic. Transvaginal US: empty uterus, 3 cm complex right adnexal mass without Doppler flow, small free fluid. IV fluids and analgesia. Gynecology at bedside; taken to the OR for laparoscopy.

Impression: right tubal ectopic pregnancy with peritoneal signs, suspected rupture. Rh positive, no anti-D needed.
Disposition: OR, then admit to gynecology.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain, no more than 6 tablets a day

reports.text:
Specimen: right fallopian tube, laparoscopic salpingectomy.
Gross: segment of fallopian tube, 5.8 cm in length, with a 2.9 cm ruptured, hemorrhagic dilatation of the ampulla; blood clot submitted separately.
Microscopic: chorionic villi and trophoblast within the tubal lumen and wall with associated hemorrhage. No hydropic change or atypical trophoblastic proliferation.
reports.conclusion: Right fallopian tube: chorionic villi with hemorrhage, consistent with tubal ectopic pregnancy.

procedures.procedure: Laparoscopic right salpingectomy for ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy

documents.title: Operative Report — Laparoscopic Right Salpingectomy
documents.author: hospital gynecology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, gynecology
Date of surgery: 10/19/2025
Preoperative diagnosis: right ectopic pregnancy, suspected rupture.
Postoperative diagnosis: ruptured right ampullary tubal ectopic pregnancy; hemoperitoneum.
Procedure: laparoscopic right salpingectomy, evacuation of hemoperitoneum.
Anesthesia: general. Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: about 300 mL of blood and clot in the pelvis. Right tube with a ruptured ampullary ectopic, actively oozing. Left tube unchanged from prior description, left in place. Both ovaries with small endometriomas, not disturbed. Scattered endometriosis on the pelvic peritoneum.

Description: three-port laparoscopy. Hemoperitoneum suctioned. Right mesosalpinx sealed and divided, tube removed in a bag. Irrigation until clear, hemostasis confirmed. No complications. To recovery in stable condition.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Gynecology
documents.author: hospital gynecology
documents.body:
Admitted 10/19/2025 from the ED; discharged 10/20/2025.
Diagnosis: ruptured right tubal ectopic pregnancy.
Procedure: laparoscopic right salpingectomy 10/19/2025.

Course: uncomplicated overnight. Pain controlled with oral medicine, tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding. Vital signs normal. Rh positive, no Rh immune globulin given.

Discharge medications: ibuprofen 600 mg every 6-8 hours as needed; acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed; prenatal vitamin.
Instructions: no lifting over 15 lb or intercourse for 2 weeks. Serum hCG weekly until negative. Gynecology office visit in 3 weeks. Return for fever, worsening pain, heavy bleeding, fainting.
Pathology pending at discharge.
Copy to primary care physician.

documents.title: In the hospital this weekend
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know, I went to the ER Sunday with terrible pain on my right side. It was an ectopic pregnancy and they had to take out my right tube. Home since yesterday. I'm okay, mostly sore and sad. They said to follow up with gyn in 3 weeks.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital this weekend
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Melissa, I'm so sorry. I'm glad you went in right away. We'll get the records from the hospital and our nurse will call you tomorrow to check on you; let's also see you in the office next week.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records request faxed to regional hospital HIM for ED visit, operative report and discharge summary 10/19-10/20/2025.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Records received this morning and reviewed with PCP. Called pt, day 3 after laparoscopic right salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic. Pain 3/10, using ibuprofen and acetaminophen, not needing anything stronger. Afebrile. Light spotting only. Incisions dry, no redness. Eating and walking fine. Husband home with her. Out of school this week. Has hCG draw scheduled with gyn next week and gyn visit 11/12. Office visit here booked 10/30. Reviewed reasons to call.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 11 days after ED visit and laparoscopic right salpingectomy for a ruptured right tubal ectopic (10/19). Records reviewed: Hgb 11.8 in the ED, ~300 mL hemoperitoneum, Rh positive. Pathology confirmed tubal ectopic.

Feeling physically much better, sore only when she twists. Spotting stopped. No fever. Using ibuprofen once a day at most, stopped acetaminophen. Back at school Monday.
Emotionally: she had noticed her period was late but hadn't tested before the pain started. Sad, some crying, sleeping okay, still enjoying her class and her husband. PHQ-9 4. No thoughts of self-harm.

Meds: ibuprofen 600 prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, a little tearful talking about it. Abdomen soft, three port sites clean, dry and healing.

A/P
1. Ruptured right tubal ectopic s/p right salpingectomy, recovering well. CBC today to see the hemoglobin recovering. hCG follow-up with gyn.
2. Grief after pregnancy loss: normal response, she has support; gave resources and invited her to reach out.
3. Endometriosis, tubal factor infertility: per op note left tube unchanged. Gyn will go over what this means for future fertility at the 11/12 visit.
4. Flu shot: wants to wait a week, nurse visit booked.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 12.4 today, up from 11.8 in the ER, so your blood count is recovering on its own. No iron needed.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine (trivalent) L deltoid. Declined COVID booster this year for now. VIS given, no reaction.

conditions.label: Right tubal pregnancy without intrauterine pregnancy

documents.title: Gynecology Post-Operative Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside OB/GYN group
Date of visit: 11/12/2025

Three weeks after laparoscopic right salpingectomy for ruptured right ampullary ectopic (performed by the hospital gynecology team). Recovering well. Port sites healed. Serum hCG on 11/10 below 5, so resolved. Pathology: chorionic villi in the right tube, consistent with ectopic.

Counseling: her right tube is gone and the left was blocked at her 2023 laparoscopy and looked the same at this surgery. Pregnancy from here would realistically mean IVF. We offered a referral back to reproductive endocrinology whenever she and her husband want it; they'd like to wait. Period pain to be managed with ibuprofen as before.

Meds: ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
OB/GYN

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit — Follow-Up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four months out from the ectopic and salpingectomy. Physically fine. Periods every 28 days, first day or two painful, ibuprofen 600 twice on those days works. No pain between, no pain with intercourse, bowels normal.
She and her husband have talked about IVF and haven't decided. "Maybe next year." Mood better, getting back to normal.

Meds: ibuprofen prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Abdomen soft, nontender, port scars healed.

A/P
1. Endometriosis with chronic pelvic pain, controlled on prn ibuprofen.
2. Tubal factor infertility, s/p right salpingectomy; IVF undecided, she knows how to reach REI.
3. Annual physical in the fall.
